To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
receptors believed responsible for the negative pressure breathing diuresis have been located by observations of the effect on urine of a stepwise expansion of the intratharacic vascular bed.
the receptors responsible for the diuretic response to negative pressure breathing are located in the left atrial appendage and in the terminal pulmonary veins.

receptors believed responsible for the effect of negative pressure breathing on urine flow have been located by observations of the effects on urine flow of the stepwise engorgment of the intratharacic vascular bed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the heart in the regulation of urine flow.
the study of the mechanisms of urine flow and its control.
the mechanisms of the kidney in the regulation of the blood volume.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the receptors which mediate the diuretic response to negative pressure breathing are located in the atria and terminal veins of the heart.
the left atrium, the terminal pulmonary veins, and probably the left ventricle are the sites of receptors which are sensitive to the active blood volume and which influence urine flow.
the receptors which mediate the diuresis associated with a negative pressure breathing are located in the left atrial region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the receptors in the atria are responsible for the diuretic response to negative-pressure breathing, but that they are probably not the receptors which initiate the response to the change in the intrathoracically circulating blood volume.
the left atrium is the site of receptors influencing urine flow.
receptors located in the atrial wall are instrumental in the mechanism linking the volume of the actively circulating blood to the homeostatic responses, especially those of the kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found a receptor that can be used as a marker to determine the location of the receptors in the atria and terminal pulmonary veins.
the left atrium, and possibly the terminal pulmonary veins, are the site of stretch receptors that influence urine flow.
the left atrial receptors play a major role in the control of the kidney.
